test_title: PYST 7: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 11 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A wholesaler offers a trade discount of 20% on a product priced at ₹10,000. On the discounted price, a scheme discount of 10% is given. However, if the customer pays in cash, an additional 5% discount is given on the final price after both discounts. How much will the customer have to pay as the final price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The final price after successive discounts can be found directly by multiplying the initial price with the respective discount multiplying factors.

Final Price = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)% × (100 − D₃)%

Final Price = 10000 × 0.80 × 0.90 × 0.95

Final Price = 10000 × 0.684 = 6840

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price of the product = ₹10,000

Trade discount (D₁) = 20%

Scheme discount (D₂) = 10%

Cash discount (D₃) = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = MP × [(100 − D₁)/100] × [(100 − D₂)/100] × [(100 − D₃)/100]

**Calculations:**

⇒ Final Selling Price = 10000 × (100 − 20)/100 × (100 − 10)/100 × (100 − 5)/100

⇒ Final Selling Price = 10000 × (80/100) × (90/100) × (95/100)

⇒ Final Selling Price = 10000 × 4/5 × 9/10 × 19/20

⇒ Final Selling Price = 10000 × (4 × 9 × 19) / (5 × 10 × 20)

⇒ Final Selling Price = 10000 × 684 / 1000

⇒ Final Selling Price = 10 × 684 = 6840

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts D₁% and D₂% are applied successively, the effective discount is given by: Dₑff = (D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂) / 100)%.

Marked Price and Selling Price

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (1 − Discount/100). The discount is always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price.

Types of Discounts

A trade discount is offered directly on the catalog price to arrive at the invoice price. A cash discount is further applied on this invoice price to encourage prompt payment.
